answer:
**Caveat:** I can't confirm the 2026 amendment text is final, and the regulation and Q&A numbering may be misremembered. Check the current consolidated Central Bank UCITS Regulations and Q&A before relying on this.

**Express 2026 approach (Reg. 26(2), as amended):**
- **Cash vs in-kind:** Cash dealing may have an earlier cut-off than in-kind, giving time to trade underlying securities.
- **Hedged vs unhedged:** Currency-hedged classes may have an earlier cut-off than unhedged ones, allowing FX hedge execution.
- **Conditions:** Cut-offs must be disclosed in the prospectus, objectively justified, and precede the valuation point. No forward-pricing breach or late trading.

**Older Q&A 1030 approach:**
- Equal treatment required one dealing deadline for all classes.
- Different deadlines needed a case-by-case Central Bank derogation on operational grounds.
- Permission came via prospectus review, not an express regulatory right.

**Express 2026 approach (Reg. 26(2), as amended):**
- **Cash vs in-kind dealing:** Cash subscriptions and redemptions may have an earlier cut-off than in-kind ones, so the fund has time to trade the underlying securities.
- **Hedged vs unhedged classes:** Class-level currency-hedged classes may have an earlier cut-off than unhedged classes, so FX hedges can be executed.
- **Conditions:** The cut-offs must be disclosed in the prospectus, be objectively justified, and stay before the valuation point. No forward-pricing breach or late trading is allowed.

**Older Q&A 1030 approach:**
- Equal treatment meant one dealing deadline for all classes.
- Different deadlines needed a case-by-case derogation from the Central Bank, based on operational justification.
- Permission came through prospectus review, not an express regulatory right.
